# Sanford Fargo unveils updated inpatient oncology unit

Nov. 12, 2025

Contact:
Nathan Aamodt
Sanford Health Media Relations
(701) 200-6080/nathan.aamodt@sanfordhealth.org

FARGO, N.D. – Sanford Health Fargo is officially opening its new inpatient oncology unit.

The 6S inpatient oncology unit, located within the Sanford Broadway Medical Center, features 16 private inpatient rooms designated to enhance patient care, comfort and efficiency. The new unit gives Sanford Fargo the capacity needed to care for more solid tumor patients and continue meeting the growing demand for services.

“We are excited to officially open our 6S inpatient oncology unit. Since 2020, patient referrals to radiation and medical oncology have increased by 54%. This unit will allow us to better accommodate the needs of our growing services,” said Susan Jarvis, Sanford Fargo chief operating officer. “This new unit signifies another incredible milestone in our journey toward transforming the Sanford Broadway campus into a modern facility designed to meet the unique needs of our patient population.”

# Grand Opening Event for New Regional Cancer Care + Prevention Center in Western North Dakota

#### McKenzie Health to Celebrate Grand Opening of Regional Cancer Care + Prevention Center

 

 

##### New center brings expanded oncology, infusion and diagnostic services closer to home for patients across western North Dakota and eastern Montana

WATFORD CITY, N.D. —For patients with cancer in western North Dakota and eastern Montana, getting specialized care no longer has to mean spending hours on the road away from home, family and support systems.

McKenzie Health will celebrate that milestone on Wednesday, October 14, from 3 to 7 p.m. with the grand opening and ribbon cutting of its new Regional Cancer Care + Prevention Center at 500 2nd Ave. SW in Watford City.

The community is invited to join McKenzie Health for an afternoon celebrating the elevation of cancer care for the region. The event will include a ribbon-cutting ceremony, hors d’oeuvres and refreshments, branded gifts for attendees and tours of the new facility, including its consultation rooms, on-site laboratory, infusion spaces, patient waiting area, and its Renewal Garden design to provide a peaceful space for reflection and respite.
Chad Pedersen. “McKenzie Health has the most experienced cancer care team in the region, and our message to patients is simple: see us first, not second. Let our team help establish the right diagnosis and treatment plan from the beginning. We can treat most patients with most cancers. Starting locally enhances coordination and reduces delays.”

With Dr. Pedersen and the McKenzie Health oncology and infusion team, patients can access a growing range of services locally, including medical oncology, hematology, chemotherapy and infusion therapies, diagnostic services and supportive care. The center also provides infusion therapy for a range of conditions beyond cancer, including autoimmune, rheumatologic, gastrointestinal, neurologic and immunologic conditions.

The new facility was designed specifically around the needs of patients and their families. Its expanded space includes dedicated oncology treatment rooms, infusion services, an on-site laboratory, satellite pharmacy, consultation rooms and improved accessibility.

“The response from our community has been incredible,” said Edis. “This facility is possible because people believed that patients in rural communities deserve access to high-quality specialty care without having to leave home. We’re proud to open the doors and invite the community in to see what they helped make possible.”

Community members, patients, families, health care providers and supporters are invited to attend the grand opening and ribbon cutting on Wednesday, October 14, from 3 to 7 p.m. at McKenzie Health Regional Cancer Care + Prevention Center, 500 2nd Ave. SW, Watford City.

For more information about oncology, infusion and cancer prevention services at McKenzie Health, call 701-842-2000 or visit McKenzieHealth.com. No referral is needed.

# Dr. Wolf-Ringwall

### DVM, PhD, DACVIM (Oncology)

Board Certified Veterinary Medical Oncologist

Oncology

Dr. Amber Wolf-Ringwall is a board-certified veterinary medical oncologist. She attended Colorado State University (CSU) where she received her BS and PhD degrees in Biomedical Sciences. Dr. Wolf developed a passion for veterinary oncology and cancer research when her two young dogs developed lymphoma during her PhD training, which led her to pursue veterinary school. She received her veterinary degree from CSU in 2014 and completed a one-year rotating internship at North Carolina State University. She then completed a 3-year medical oncology residency at the CSU Flint Animal Cancer Center.

Dr. Wolf moved to Minnesota in 2018 to join the oncology team at the University of Minnesota. She served as a clinical assistant professor, enjoying roles in teaching, research, and leadership as the section head of the clinical oncology service. In 2023, Dr. Wolf explored various locum opportunities around the country in both academia and private practice to broaden her perspective and gain real-world experience. She then had the honor of joining the Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center in Fargo to establish the first veterinary oncology practice for pets in her home state of North Dakota.

Dr. Wolf has a special interest in hematologic cancers such as lymphoma/leukemia, cytology and molecular diagnostic tests, clinical trials, comparative oncology, and in helping families navigate their pet’s cancer journey. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her husband and their dogs Violet and Sisu, hiking and enjoying nature, traveling, cheering on the Denver Broncos, watching Formula 1 races, attending concerts, and exploring the Twin Cities with family and friends.

# CHI Williston to begin offering oncology services in September

CHI Williston President Garrick Hyde said the hospital will have more access to service in the region through its own program.

By Michael Anthony

Published: Aug. 19, 2024 at 5:26 PM CDT

Share

WILLISTON, N.D. (KUMV) - CHI St. Alexius Williston will be providing its own oncology services starting next month.

Previously, those services were handled by medical oncologists from Billings Clinic a few times a month but stopped earlier this year over staffing issues.

CHI Williston President Garrick Hyde said the hospital will have more access to service in the region through its own program.

“We will have coverage from our M.D.’s at least six days a month and advance practice providers, which are nurse practitioners that are specialized in oncology three days a week, which we didn’t have before,” said Hyde.

Dr. Michael Grant, a radiation oncologist with CHI, said the local program can triple the hospital’s capacity for medical oncology needs.

“It means more capacity. It means quicker referrals, faster appointments and more access to care for northwestern North Dakota and northeastern Montana. There’s quite a few folks in the Hi-Line of Montana that we also serve, so it will be better for them,” said Grant.

Hyde said the program starts Sept. 4 at the Leonard P. Nelson Cancer Center.

He adds the facility is equipped with the most advanced technology when it comes to cancer treatment and a scalp cooling system to minimize hair loss during chemotherapy.
